lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Bagong dating ka, ano? Akala ko ikaw yung guro na hinihintay namin galing Maynila.
lines.translation: You're new here, huh? I thought you were the teacher we were expecting from Manila.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Sige, sabay ka — pero huwag mo munang banggitin ang pangalang Ibarra nang malakas ngayong araw, ha?
lines.translation: Come along — but best not to mention the name Ibarra too loudly today.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Kagabi, may dinner sa bahay ni Capitán Tiago para sa pagbabalik ni Ibarra galing Europa. Ang sabi, pumunta si Padre Dámaso at... nagpakita ng hindi magandang ugali.
lines.translation: Last night, there was a dinner at Capitán Tiago's house for Ibarra's return from Europe. They say Padre Dámaso attended and... showed very bad behavior.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mang Tenyo gives you a knowing look. Whatever happened with the Ibarra family, it's clearly still fresh in people's minds. Your cover as a visiting scholar's aide begins now.

lines.speaker: Aling Nena
lines.text: Nakita mo ba? Bumalik na si Ginoong Ibarra galing Europa — pitong taon, ha!
lines.translation: Did you see? Mr. Ibarra has returned from Europe — seven years, huh!

lines.speaker: Mang Andres
lines.text: Oo, pero nakita mo rin ba ang mukha ni Padre Dámaso kagabi? Parang gustong sabunutan ang bata sa harap ng lahat.
lines.translation: Yes, but did you also see Padre Dámaso's face last night? Like he wanted to attack the young man right in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: Aling Nena
lines.text: Kawawa naman si Capitán Tiago — nag-host pa ng magandang dinner, tapos ginulo ni Padre Dámaso.
lines.translation: Poor Capitán Tiago — he even hosted a nice dinner, and then Padre Dámaso ruined it.

lines.speaker: Mang Andres
lines.text: Hindi ba malapit sila dati? Ang Padre Dámaso at ang ama ni Ibarra?
lines.translation: Weren't they close before? Padre Dámaso and Ibarra's father?

lines.speaker: Aling Nena
lines.text: Oo nga, Don Rafael at Padre Dámaso — magkaibigan daw sila noon. Pero pagkatapos ng kamatayan ni Don Rafael, bigla nagbago ang ugali ng Padre. Kataka-taka.
lines.translation: Yes, Don Rafael and Padre Dámaso — they were friends, they say. But after Don Rafael's death, the Padre suddenly changed his attitude. Strange.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gossip fades as you step away. You now understand why Mang Tenyo warned you — Ibarra's return has stirred up old tensions between the friars and the Filipino community. The Spanish friars clearly see educated Filipinos as a threat to their power.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next morning, the plaza is quieter. A light breeze carries the scent of fresh bread from the market stalls. The fountain's water glints in the early light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A young man in a fine coat crosses the plaza, greeting the vendors with an ease that doesn't quite match the tension you overheard about last night. He pauses near the fountain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That must be Crisóstomo Ibarra. After seven years in Europe, he looks like someone who has seen the world beyond these streets — and perhaps carries ideas that the friars would rather he didn't.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You've now witnessed the key players of this story: the returning ilustrado, the hostile friar, and the anxious host. Chapter 1 is complete. Time to test what you've learned.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Mabuti nandito ka rin. Kumakalat na ang tsismis tungkol sa reception kagabi. Ang sabi, insulto daw ang ginawa ni Padre Dámaso sa harap ng lahat.
lines.translation: Good you're here. Gossip about last night's reception is spreading. They say Padre Dámaso insulted Ibarra in front of everyone.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Pumunta ka sa market area — may mga kusinera doon na nag-uusap. Baka makakuha ka ng impormasyon kung ano talaga ang nangyari.
lines.translation: Go to the market area — kitchen staff are talking there. You might learn what really happened.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Narinig mo na ang tsismis? Mag-ingat ka pa rin. Ang mga Prayle, may malaking poder dito — hindi lang espiritu, kundi pati pulitika at ekonomiya.
lines.translation: You heard the gossip? Be careful still. The Friars have great power here — not just spiritual, but also political and economic.

lines.speaker: Mang Tenyo
lines.text: Ang mga ilustrado na nag-aral sa Europa, tulad ni Ibarra, ang nagdadala ng ideya na nakakabahala sa mga Prayle. Kaya galit sila.
lines.translation: The ilustrados who studied in Europe, like Ibarra, bring ideas that worry the Friars. That's why they're angry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Mang Tenyo's words echo what you've learned from the gossip. The friars see educated Filipinos as a threat — and Ibarra's return from Europe has made that tension visible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: You find yourself at the edge of a town you don't recognize. The year, you'll soon learn, is 1887.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The air smells different here — earth and woodsmoke, no car exhaust. The buildings are low, the streets unpaved. A fountain bubbles in the center of the plaza. And somehow, you feel like you've read about this place before...
